q: How do I calculate a tram's CO2 per passenger km?
title: Tram CO2 per passenger km
short: Take traction electricity from the substations feeding the overhead line, multiply by 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, and divide by passenger km. Depot and workshop power are separate lines. Low ridership on a route raises the per passenger figure sharply.
audience: Tram operators and urban transport researchers

ul: Traction substation meters for the network.
Ticket data and average trip length.

p: Use the same occupancy basis when you compare a tram with buses on the same corridor.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
